executiveSummary: Analysis of 21 surveillance reports from ECDC and PAHO spanning October 2025 through May 2026 reveals multiple concurrent biological threats across the Americas and Europe. The most pressing concerns include ongoing Avian Influenza A(H5N1) activity in the Americas with zoonotic spillover risk, a resurgent dengue season, and the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season coinciding with RSV circulation. Pertussis is demonstrating sustained elevated transmission across the Americas region, while mpox continues to circulate with updated epidemiological data reported as recently as April 2026.
bottomLine: Multiple simultaneous epidemic threats—including H5N1, dengue, mpox, pertussis, and seasonal influenza—are active across the Americas and Europe, requiring coordinated surveillance and response measures.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained H5N1 activity
Zoonotic spillover risk to humans from animal reservoirs across the Americas
Dual categorization as both animal and human threat reflecting cross-species transmission concern
threats.action: Enhance animal-human interface surveillance, activate zoonotic disease response protocols, ensure stockpiling of antiviral countermeasures, and issue guidance to at-risk agricultural workers

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued February 2026 indicating active transmission
Historically high dengue burden in Americas with hyperendemic multi-serotype circulation
Seasonal patterns suggest ongoing escalation into mid-2026
threats.action: Strengthen vector control operations, activate case management surge capacity, enhance serotype surveillance, and issue public health communications targeting high-burden countries

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza / Respiratory Virus Co-circulation
threats.location: Americas Region (Southern Hemisphere and Northern Hemisphere)
signals: PAHO alert issued April 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere influenza season
January 2026 alert flagging simultaneous influenza and RSV circulation
December 2025 alert tracking end of Southern Hemisphere season and start of Northern Hemisphere 2025-26 season indicating continuous global burden
threats.action: Promote influenza vaccination uptake, prepare healthcare systems for respiratory surge, monitor for novel reassortant strains, and coordinate hemisphere-specific seasonal guidance

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained elevated transmission
Multi-country resurgence pattern consistent with post-pandemic immunity gap
Vulnerable populations including infants and unvaccinated individuals at high risk
threats.action: Reinforce vaccination coverage especially for infants and pregnant women, investigate vaccine hesitancy drivers, enhance laboratory confirmation capacity, and issue clinical guidance for healthcare providers

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 2026 indicating continued regional transmission
Ongoing surveillance updates suggest the outbreak has not been contained
Risk of further spread in populations with low vaccine coverage
threats.action: Accelerate mpox vaccination in high-risk populations, strengthen contact tracing infrastructure, ensure diagnostic capacity, and maintain cross-border surveillance coordination

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 2026 indicating active risk
Sylvatic transmission cycle remains active in endemic zones
Risk of urban spread in areas with Aedes aegypti vectors and low vaccination coverage
threats.action: Enforce mandatory vaccination requirements for travel to endemic areas, conduct emergency vaccination campaigns in at-risk unvaccinated populations, and enhance epizootics monitoring in non-human primates

threats.name: Chikungunya
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026
Co-circulation with dengue increases diagnostic confusion and healthcare burden
Expanding vector range of Aedes albopictus elevates risk of spread to new areas
threats.action: Implement integrated vector management, differentiate diagnostically from dengue, monitor for novel genotype introductions, and prepare clinical care guidelines for chronic chikungunya arthropathy

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 2026 indicating active cases
Post-pandemic immunity gaps and vaccine hesitancy creating susceptible cohorts
Risk of importation events into previously elimination-certified countries
threats.action: Audit measles vaccination coverage at subnational level, conduct catch-up immunization campaigns for missed children, strengthen outbreak investigation capacity, and reinforce measles elimination status monitoring

diseases: Communicable disease threats (ECDC weekly reports - multiple pathogens)

amrSignals: No explicit AMR reports identified in the provided surveillance titles; however, pertussis resurgence in vaccinated populations warrants investigation into potential macrolide treatment failures
Sustained multi-pathogen co-circulation increases empirical antibiotic use risk, potentially driving secondary AMR pressure in the Americas and Europe
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen respiratory co-circulation (influenza, RSV, pertussis) in both hemispheres suggesting strained healthcare capacity windows
Post-pandemic immunity debt driving resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases including measles and pertussis across the Americas
Sustained H5N1 activity in animals with repeated PAHO updates over a 4-month window indicating enzootic establishment rather than isolated spillover events
Arboviral triple threat—dengue, chikungunya, and yellow fever—co-circulating in overlapping geographic zones with shared Aedes vector populations
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly communicable disease threat reports in April-May 2026 suggesting heightened European surveillance alert posture
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse flagged as a public health concern by PAHO, representing an emerging non-communicable iatrogenic risk signal
